summary: Implement provider-neutral immutable Order/OrderItem snapshots, normalized lifecycle, exact money/quantity/tax facts, generic external order mapping, optimistic concurrency, and atomic audit + transactional-outbox intent without provider statuses in Core.

impacts.evidence: Orders and OrderItems carry organization/workspace ownership, composite tenant foreign keys, forced RLS, and tenant-scoped repository transactions.
Task 006 deliberately stores no customer PII/address in the baseline aggregate; audit/events contain commerce identifiers and totals only.
New Draft 2020-12 Order/OrderItem contracts establish provider-neutral v1 shapes; the legacy order_created.v1 contract is left untouched.
New commerce.orders.order_changed.v1 is additive and emitted through Task-008 Transactional Outbox; existing order_created.v1 is retained unchanged.
Provider status translation and remote order IDs remain connector concerns; generic connector_entity_mappings is broadened only to entity_type=order.
Atomic expand migration 000011 adds immutable order snapshots/RLS/totals guards and broadens the mapping type constraint without rewriting earlier migration files.
Immutable commercial snapshots, exact non-negative money, positive exact quantities, tax bounds, lifecycle triggers, tenant FKs and hard-delete blockers fail closed.
Task 006 records canonical order state; provider-facing writes remain behind later connector approval/dry-run boundaries.
Create/status transitions append immutable Task-003 audit records in the same SQL transaction as order state and outbox intent.
Stable order IDs, optimistic versions, immutable item snapshots and generic remote mappings provide deterministic inputs for Tasks 013/014; Inbox remains consumer duplicate protection.
Versioned order_changed events and bounded audit summaries expose lifecycle mutation signals without provider payloads or PII.
Migration 000011 is additive; rollback disables new order writers while retaining immutable order/audit/outbox history.
Unit/migration/contract/rehearsal tests cover lifecycle, exact totals, tax inclusion, provider neutrality, mapping expansion, RLS and restore paths.
